g.text: N1 [Context]
VLA models for generalist robot policies
Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as a promising paradigm for
building generalist robot policies that can interpret natural language
instructions and execute complex manipulation tasks (Brohan et al., 2022;
2023; Kim et al.,…
g.title: N1 [Context] (cites=4) Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as a promising paradigm for building generalist robot policies that can interpret natural language instructions and execute complex manipulation tasks (Brohan et al., 2022; 2023; Kim et al., 2024; Black et al., 2024).

g.text: N2 [Context]
VLMs transfer semantic knowledge to control
By leveraging pretrained vision-language models, these systems can transfer
semantic knowledge from web-scale data to robotic control, enabling more
flexible and generalizable robot behaviors.
g.title: N2 [Context] (cites=0) By leveraging pretrained vision-language models, these systems can transfer semantic knowledge from web-scale data to robotic control, enabling more flexible and generalizable robot behaviors.

g.text: N3 [Limitation]
Standard VLAs have fixed compute depth
A key limitation of standard VLA architectures is their fixed
computational depth: the same amount of compute is expended
regardless of task complexity.
g.title: N3 [Limitation] (cites=0) A key limitation of standard VLA architectures is their fixed computational depth: the same amount of compute is expended regardless of task complexity.

g.text: N4 [Prior_Work : ANCHOR]
RD-VLA: recurrent action head
RD-VLA (Tur et al., 2026) addresses this by introducing a recurrent action
head that enables test-time compute scaling through iterative latent
refinement.
g.title: N4 [Prior_Work] (cites=1) RD-VLA (Tur et al., 2026) addresses this by introducing a recurrent action head that enables test-time compute scaling through iterative latent refinement.

g.text: N5 [Prior_Work]
Weight-tied unrolling to depth K
By unrolling a weight-tied transformer block to arbitrary depth K, RD-VLA
can dynamically allocate compute based on task difficulty, achieving
significant improvements on challenging manipulation tasks.
g.title: N5 [Prior_Work] (cites=0) By unrolling a weight-tied transformer block to arbitrary depth K, RD-VLA can dynamically allocate compute based on task difficulty, achieving significant improvements on challenging manipulation tasks.

g.text: N6 [Limitation]
Depth boundary degrades performance at K>24
However, RD-VLA reports a "depth boundary" phenomenon where
performance degrades at high iteration counts (K > 24), limiting
the practical utility of depth extrapolation.
g.title: N6 [Limitation] (cites=0) However, RD-VLA reports a "depth boundary" phenomenon where performance degrades at high iteration counts (K > 24), limiting the practical utility of depth extrapolation.

g.text: N7 [Limitation]
Iterative frameworks share instability issue
This instability resembles challenges observed in other iterative
computation frameworks, such as Deep Equilibrium Models (DEQ) (Bai et al.,
2019) and Universal Transformers (Dehghani et al., 2018), where unbounded
iteration can lead to…
g.title: N7 [Limitation] (cites=2) This instability resembles challenges observed in other iterative computation frameworks, such as Deep Equilibrium Models (DEQ) (Bai et al., 2019) and Universal Transformers (Dehghani et al., 2018), where unbounded iteration can lead to divergent or oscillatory behavior.

g.text: N8 [Method]
Jacobian regularization for contractive dynamics
We investigate Jacobian regularization (Bai et al., 2021) as a principled
approach to encourage contractive dynamics in the RD-VLA recurrent core.
g.title: N8 [Method] (cites=1) We investigate Jacobian regularization (Bai et al., 2021) as a principled approach to encourage contractive dynamics in the RD-VLA recurrent core.

g.text: N9 [Method]
Frobenius-norm penalty guarantees contraction
By penalizing the Frobenius norm of the state-to-state Jacobian, we aim to
ensure that the recurrent mapping is a contraction, guaranteeing convergence
to a unique fixed point regardless of iteration depth.
g.title: N9 [Method] (cites=0) By penalizing the Frobenius norm of the state-to-state Jacobian, we aim to ensure that the recurrent mapping is a contraction, guaranteeing convergence to a unique fixed point regardless of iteration depth.

g.text: N10 [Result]
Depth boundary absent on LIBERO-10
Surprisingly, our experiments on LIBERO-10 (Liu et al., 2023) reveal that
the depth boundary phenomenon does not manifest in this setting.
g.title: N10 [Result] (cites=1) Surprisingly, our experiments on LIBERO-10 (Liu et al., 2023) reveal that the depth boundary phenomenon does not manifest in this setting.

g.text: N11 [Result]
0% overthinking, flat MSE K=4..128
Both baseline and Jacobian-regularized RD-VLA exhibit 0% overthinking with
flat MSE curves across depths K = 4 to K = 128.
g.title: N11 [Result] (cites=0) Both baseline and Jacobian-regularized RD-VLA exhibit 0% overthinking with flat MSE curves across depths K = 4 to K = 128.

g.text: N12 [Result]
Depth boundary is benchmark-specific
This suggests that the depth boundary may be benchmark-specific or
evaluation-protocol-dependent, rather than an inherent limitation of the
architecture.
g.title: N12 [Result] (cites=0) This suggests that the depth boundary may be benchmark-specific or evaluation-protocol-dependent, rather than an inherent limitation of the architecture.

g.text: C1 [Contribution: Finding 1]
Finding 1: benchmark-specific depth boundary
Empirical evidence of benchmark-specific depth boundary: We
demonstrate that the overthinking phenomenon reported in RD-VLA
does not occur on LIBERO-10 with offline teacher-forced
evaluation, informing future research on when and why depth…
g.title: C1 [Contribution: Finding 1] (cites=0) Empirical evidence of benchmark-specific depth boundary: We demonstrate that the overthinking phenomenon reported in RD-VLA does not occur on LIBERO-10 with offline teacher-forced evaluation, informing future research on when and why depth boundaries manifest.

g.text: C2 [Contribution: Finding 2]
Finding 2: two-phase training, 1.6% MSE, 15x
Two-phase training for Jacobian regularization: We propose a
training strategy that achieves 1.6% MSE improvement with 15×
efficiency gain over from-scratch regularization, by fine-tuning a
converged baseline with gentle Jacobian penalty.
g.title: C2 [Contribution: Finding 2] (cites=0) Two-phase training for Jacobian regularization: We propose a training strategy that achieves 1.6% MSE improvement with 15× efficiency gain over from-scratch regularization, by fine-tuning a converged baseline with gentle Jacobian penalty.

g.text: C3 [Contribution: Finding 3]
Finding 3: 6-iter convergence, 50% compute savings
Adaptive stopping analysis: We show that the RD-VLA recurrent core
converges within 6 iterations on average, enabling 50% compute
savings at inference through early termination.
g.title: C3 [Contribution: Finding 3] (cites=0) Adaptive stopping analysis: We show that the RD-VLA recurrent core converges within 6 iterations on average, enabling 50% compute savings at inference through early termination.
